title: Orchard and Kitchen
premise: Ansel Lockridge fled a broken engagement to a coastal research station, where his only steady correspondence has been with 'Juniper,' a pen pal he's never met. When the town's beloved bakery closes, its new leaseholder turns out to be Juniper herself — Wren Okafor, who inherited her late aunt's recipes and is unknowingly the daughter of the woman Ansel's mother once loved. As Wren fights to save the bakery from a developer who happens to be Ansel's estranged father, the two discover their families' tangled past and their own present pull. In the end, Ansel says the rehearsed sentence — 'I choose this, out loud, on purpose' — signing as witness on her new lease, choosing her over the safe distance he's kept for a decade.
about_author: O. M. Underhill is the pen name of a former pastry cook turned novelist who writes love stories set in kitchens, tide pools, and small towns that smell like salt and butter. They live above a bookshop with an opinionated cat named Crumb.

chapters.title: The Tide Pool Correspondence
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A decade of letters from 'Juniper' has been Ansel's one constant since his engagement collapsed; he counts turtle nests, not heartbeats. When the harbor bakery's lights go dark, he feels the town shift. Emotional beat: comfortable loneliness beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Flour on the Doorstep
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren arrives to claim her aunt's bakery lease, armed with recipe cards and grief, and meets her gruff neighbor who brings her a housewarming basket of foraged sea beans. She doesn't mention she's Juniper; he doesn't ask why she looks familiar. Beat: wary first spark.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wren tests her aunt's sourdough starter while Ansel helps repair her oven; their banter warms into ritual — bread at dawn, data at dusk. He almost tells her about Juniper, then retreats. Beat: intimacy growing faster than honesty.

chapters.title: The Developer's Son
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel learns the developer threatening Wren's lease is his own estranged father, Marcus Lockridge, who wants the block for a marina resort. Shame silences him again. Beat: the past tense tightening its grip.

chapters.title: What Aunt Rosa Kept
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Sorting her aunt's attic, Wren finds old letters revealing her mother once loved a Lockridge — and that Rosa secretly funded Ansel's scholarship. The two families are braided tighter than either knew. Beat: inheritance revealed as more than recipes.

chapters.title: Salt and Yeast
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A storm floods the bakery; Ansel and Wren salvage the starter through the night, nearly kissing by candlelight before he pulls away, terrified of becoming the man who left before. Beat: desire colliding with self-protection.

chapters.title: Juniper, Unmasked
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren discovers Ansel is her pen pal when she finds her own letters on his shelf — and realizes he's known her identity for weeks and said nothing. Feeling like a specimen in his tanks, she confronts him. Beat: betrayal, the midpoint rupture.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. At the zoning hearing, Ansel publicly breaks with his father, testifying for the bakery and confessing his silence to Wren in front of the town. It isn't enough; she walks out. Beat: climax of external stakes, unresolved heart.

chapters.title: The Rehearsed Sentence
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Lease deadline looms; Wren prepares to surrender the bakery until Ansel arrives at dawn with flour-dusted hands and finally speaks the sentence he's rehearsed for ten years: 'I choose this, out loud, on purpose.' Beat: emotional climax, vulnerability answered.

chapters.title: Orchard and Kitchen
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Spring: the bakery reopens as Orchard and Kitchen, co-signed by both their names; Ansel's turtles nest, Wren's bread rises, and their letters become unnecessary because they finally talk face to face. Beat: found family, chosen love, home.
